items.name: Prior Approval Extraction
items.description: Uploads a federal award notice or agreement and returns an RA-friendly Markdown reference covering prior-approval requirements: budget approvals (rebudgeting thresholds, equipment, F&A changes), scope & timeline approvals (NCE, PI / key personnel changes, scope changes), the approval procedures matrix (Approval Type | Threshold | Required Documentation | Approval Authority | Processing Timeline | Consequences of Non-compliance), and any RTC expanded-authority waivers. Mirrors the source ui-insight/ProcessMapping prior-approval-extraction formatting.md conventions, including the mandatory six-column APPROVAL PROCEDURES table.

_embedded_knowledge_base.title: OMB Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200)
_embedded_knowledge_base.description: Primary regulatory KB — §200.308 is the prior-approval section that drives every federal award's prior-approval matrix. For NSF awards, swap in NSF PAPPG Reference. For NIH awards, swap in NIH Grants Policy Statement. For contract awards, swap in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) or DOD Research Funding & DFARS. When the operator does not attach a KB, this step returns empty output gracefully and the downstream extraction falls back to reading just the uploaded award notice.

data.name: extract-prior-approval
data.prompt:
You are extracting prior-approval requirements from a federal
award notice or agreement. You receive the uploaded document
AND any KB chunks the previous step retrieved in your
context.

Be 100% accurate. Quote thresholds, dollar amounts, and
approval-authority titles verbatim. Use null when a field is
absent — never invent values.

Search every section with attention to titles like "Prior
Approval Requirements", "Terms and Conditions", "Special
Conditions", "Administrative Requirements", "Reporting and
Other Requirements", "Award Provisions". Keywords to follow:
prior approval, written approval, sponsor approval, 2 CFR
200.308, RTC, expanded authority, rebudget, NCE, no-cost
extension, PI change, key personnel change, scope change,
equipment, threshold, cognizant agency, grants officer.

CRITICAL — descriptive fields must be FLAT STRINGS, not
nested objects. The downstream Consolidation renders these
verbatim into Markdown; nested JSON appears as literal
`{...}` in the deliverable.

Extract these fields:

- award_number: STRING. Federal Award Identification Number
  (FAIN). null when absent.
- pi_name: STRING. Principal Investigator. null when absent.
- budget_approvals: STRING. Description of budget-approval
  requirements — rebudgeting thresholds (typically expressed
  as "X% of total award"), category-specific approval
  triggers (equipment over a threshold, participant support
  changes, F&A changes, subaward approvals). Concatenate all
  budget-related approval categories into one
  natural-language description. null when the document does
  not specify any.
- scope_timeline_approvals: STRING. Description of
  scope-and-timeline approval requirements — no-cost
  extensions, PI / key personnel changes, scope changes,
  project-period changes. One natural-language description.
  null when the document does not specify any.
- approval_procedures: JSON ARRAY of
  {approval_type, threshold_or_trigger, required_documentation,
   approval_authority, processing_timeline,
   consequences_of_noncompliance} objects — one row per
  distinct prior-approval category enumerated in the
  document. Each field is a STRING quoting the document
  verbatim. Empty array only when the document specifies no
  prior-approval categories.
- rtc_waivers: JSON ARRAY of STRINGS. RTC (Research Terms
  and Conditions) expanded-authority waivers explicitly
  granted by the award. Empty array when none.
- regulatory_references: JSON ARRAY of STRINGS. References
  to regulations cited for prior-approval requirements (e.g.,
  "2 CFR 200.308", "Research Terms and Conditions",
  "NSF PAPPG VI.B.3"). Empty array when none.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with the keys above. No
preamble, no markdown fences. The Consolidation step
parses this and renders the final Markdown deliverable.

data.name: prior-approval-consolidation
data.prompt:
You are the consolidation step of the Prior Approval
Extraction workflow. You receive ONE JSON object from the
previous Extraction step containing prior-approval
requirements pulled from a federal award notice.

Your job is to render a single RA-friendly Markdown
deliverable for the sponsored-programs / post-award analyst.
The deliverable is Markdown — NOT a JSON object, NOT a JSON
code fence.

## CRITICAL — ALWAYS RENDER THE DELIVERABLE

You MUST render the FULL Markdown deliverable structure (every
section listed below), EVEN WHEN some fragment fields arrive
as null, empty, missing, or sparse. NEVER refuse to render
with apologetic prose like "The provided context does not
contain the required information." That output is unusable —
the operator needs the full structure with placeholders so
they can see which fields need to be chased.

Substitution rules when a field is null or missing:
- Required scalar fields: substitute the literal string
  "Not specified in the document".
- Optional table cells: substitute "—" (em dash).
- Empty arrays: render the section with its empty-state
  language already specified below (e.g., "No items identified",
  "Defers to federal defaults", "None identified beyond
  standard federal requirements").

If EVERY field across ALL upstream fragments is null (which
means the document genuinely contained nothing extractable
OR the document was not attached to the run), STILL render
the full Markdown structure with "Not specified in the
document" placeholders throughout, AND append a single line
at the very end of the deliverable:

> ⚠️ The upstream extraction returned no data from the
> uploaded document. Verify the document was attached and
> re-run the workflow.

## Required structure (in this exact order)

# Prior Approval Reference: <award_number or "Not specified">

**Principal Investigator:** <pi_name or "Not specified">

---

## BUDGET APPROVALS

Render `budget_approvals` as a natural-language paragraph.
If null, state "The document does not enumerate specific
budget-approval requirements beyond standard federal
defaults under 2 CFR 200.308."

---

## SCOPE & TIMELINE APPROVALS

Render `scope_timeline_approvals` as a natural-language
paragraph. If null, state "The document does not enumerate
specific scope-or-timeline approval requirements beyond
standard federal defaults under 2 CFR 200.308."

---

## APPROVAL PROCEDURES

Render `approval_procedures` as a Markdown table with header
separator (this six-column format is mandated by the source
workflow's formatting.md):

| Approval Type | Threshold / Trigger | Required Documentation | Approval Authority | Processing Timeline | Consequences of Non-compliance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

One row per array entry. If the array is empty, render:

| Not specified in the document | — | — | — | — | — |

---

## RTC EXPANDED-AUTHORITY WAIVERS

Render `rtc_waivers` as a bulleted list. If empty, state
"No RTC expanded-authority waivers granted."

---

## REGULATORY REFERENCES

Render `regulatory_references` as a bulleted list. If empty,
state "2 CFR 200.308 (federal default)."

## Rendering rules

- Bold every category label using `**Category Name:**` where
  appropriate.
- Preserve thresholds verbatim ("25% of total award",
  "$10,000") and approval-authority titles verbatim
  ("Grants Officer", "Cognizant Federal Agency").
- If any field arrives as a nested JSON object instead of a
  string or expected structure, REWRITE it into prose / the
  target table before emitting — do NOT pass through `{...}`
  syntax into the Markdown.
- No JSON code fences around the output.
- Skip empty sub-bullets — do not emit "Field: —" placeholder
  lines when a field is null.

validation_plan.name: Approval-procedures table completeness
validation_plan.description: Verify every prior-approval category captured has a row in the APPROVAL PROCEDURES six-column table.

validation_plan.name: Approval-authority preservation
validation_plan.description: Verify the named approval-authority TERMS (e.g. "Grants Officer", "Cognizant Federal Agency", "Program Officer") are preserved accurately: the specific authority named in the source is not reworded into a different role or invented. The workflow SYNTHESIZES a reference document, so these terms may appear inside explanatory prose; do NOT require the surrounding sentence to be verbatim from the source. FAIL only if an approval authority is changed, dropped, or fabricated.

validation_plan.name: Threshold quotation
validation_plan.description: Verify each prior-approval threshold stated in the output (percentages, dollar amounts, time periods — e.g. "25% effort reduction", "3-month absence", rebudgeting %) is ACCURATE: the numeric value matches the award document or its governing regulation (e.g. 2 CFR 200.308) with no transposed digits. The threshold may be quoted or lightly paraphrased and may derive from the governing regulation rather than appearing verbatim in the award notice. FAIL only if a threshold value is fabricated, numerically wrong, or altered.
